user.title: Connect to a Meterkat companion
user.description: Run `meterkat pair` on the machine that runs the companion. Pairing gives Home Assistant its own access, which you can revoke later with `meterkat devices`.

menu_options.url: Enter the companion's URL and a pairing code
menu_options.legacy_token: Older companion: host, port and token

pairing_link.title: Paste a pairing link
pairing_link.description: Paste the `meterkat://pair?...` link from `meterkat pair`. It works once, for 5 minutes. Home Assistant tries the local address first, then the remote one.

url.title: Companion URL and pairing code
url.description: Use this when Home Assistant reaches the companion at an address that isn't in the pairing link, such as an HTTPS reverse proxy. Paste the pairing link, or just its `code=` value, from `meterkat pair`.

data_description.url: For example `http://192.168.1.20:47300` or `https://meterkat.example.com`. A bare host uses port 47300.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only for a self-signed certificate you trust. Better: give the CA file below.
data_description.ca_file: Optional path to a PEM file, such as `/config/certs/my-ca.pem`, that signed the proxy's certificate.

legacy_token.title: Older companion
legacy_token.description: Companions before 2.5.0 can't pair devices individually. Enter the address and the shared token (`token` in `~/.config/meterkat/config.json`). Better: update the companion with `meterkat update`, then add it with a pairing link.

data_description.host: The companion's LAN address or hostname, for example 192.168.1.20.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Set up {name}
zeroconf_confirm.description: Home Assistant found a Meterkat companion at {url}. Run `meterkat pair` on that machine and paste the pairing link or its `code=` value.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect to the Meterkat companion
reauth_confirm.description: The companion at {host} no longer accepts Home Assistant's access, perhaps because it was revoked or the shared token was rotated. Run `meterkat pair` on it and paste the pairing link or code.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Meterkat
reconfigure.description: Change the address or certificate settings. To move off the companion's shared token, run `meterkat pair` and paste the pairing link or code; leave it empty to keep the current access.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the companion. Check the address and that `meterkat status` shows it running.
error.invalid_link: That is not a Meterkat pairing link. It starts with `meterkat://pair?`.
error.invalid_url: Enter an http:// or https:// address.
error.pairing_failed: The pairing code is wrong, has expired or was already used. Run `meterkat pair` again.
error.not_meterkat: Something answered, but it isn't a Meterkat companion.
error.companion_too_old: This companion is older than 2.5.0 and can't pair devices individually. Update it with `meterkat update`, or use the older-companion option.
error.ssl_error: The HTTPS certificate isn't trusted. Provide the CA file, or turn off certificate verification.
error.missing_credentials: Enter a pairing code or link, or a token.

abort.already_configured: This companion is already set up.
abort.wrong_companion: That belongs to a different companion.
abort.companion_too_old: This companion is older than 2.5.0. Update it with `meterkat update`, then add it again.

shared_token.title: {name} uses the companion's shared token
shared_token.description: This entry still uses the shared token that older apps use, so it can't be revoked on its own. Run `meterkat pair` on the companion, then open the integration, choose **Reconfigure**, and paste the pairing link. Home Assistant then gets its own token, listed in `meterkat devices`.

init.title: Meterkat options
init.description: Home Assistant waits for the companion's next snapshot (the companion polls the providers every 120 seconds), so it never causes extra provider calls.
